answer: Each identity locks 70 credits in the umber ledger and issues 30-day invoices. A wander visit signed on site collects one invoice; signatures cannot be reused. The summit board publishes aging buckets recomputed from invoice dates; receivables over 30 days old without a visit burn the bond. Visits book in ledger order, so the k-th visit costs 20+2(k-1) credits; 1,000 fakes pay 1,019,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-collection ring fails: a visit at the wrong site or customer is rejected and burns the bond. An honest agent pays 70 plus 20 once, recovering it after a clean epoch.
